Effective sample size of the IPW weights

ess_weights.Rd

Computes the Kish effective sample size of the weights \(1 / \hat\pi(W, Y, Z)\) among the uncensored rows, \((\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2\), and reports it as a fraction of the number of uncensored rows. In the manuscript's simulations, the IPW and unguarded AIPW estimators had small bias and near-nominal coverage when this fraction was at least about 65\ at least about 80\ for \(X | Z\) is credible.

Usage

ess_weights(data_yXZ, model_weights)

Arguments

data_yXZ

A data frame with W, D, and the variables in model_weights.

model_weights

A one-sided formula for the Weibull AFT model of \(C | (Y, Z)\), e.g. ~ y + Z.

Value

A list with ess (effective sample size), ess_frac

(ess divided by the number of uncensored rows), n_uncensored, max_weight, and max_weight_share (largest weight over the sum of the weights).

Examples

set.seed(1)
dat <- data_aft(1000, c_int = -1.5)   # about 85% right-censoring
ess_weights(dat, ~ y + Z)
#> $ess
#> [1] 69.28943
#> 
#> $ess_frac
#> [1] 0.4499314
#> 
#> $n_uncensored
#> [1] 154
#> 
#> $max_weight
#> [1] 64.91956
#> 
#> $max_weight_share
#> [1] 0.0664769
#>
